facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object, for construction, mining, quarrying and similar work.
facts.quote: already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer is developing a system that automatically applies the brakes if the operator does not react.
facts.quote: developing a system that also applies the brakes automatically if the operator does not react

facts.text: Prototype hardware and software for the heavy off-road machine braking system will arrive in mid-2027.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software will arrive in mid-2027

facts.text: Validation of the new heavy off-road machine braking system must finish in less than four months after prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software will arrive in mid-2027, and validation must then finish in less than four months

facts.text: Validation previously took three to four years of mostly physical testing and tuning per heavy off-road machine model.
facts.quote: it used to take three to four years of mostly physical testing and tuning per machine model

facts.text: The new heavy off-road machine braking system must work across more than 100 types of job site.
facts.quote: The new system must work across more than 100 types of job site

facts.text: The new heavy off-road machine braking system must work across more than 10 operating scenarios per machine.
facts.quote: more than 10 operating scenarios per machine

facts.text: The new heavy off-road machine braking system must work in many weather and light conditions, including rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness and glare.
facts.quote: many weather and light conditions (rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness, glare)

facts.text: The new heavy off-road machine braking system must work across many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.
facts.quote: many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions

facts.text: Sensor types for the new heavy off-road machine braking system are not confirmed, so the virtual-environment research had to cover camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other options.
facts.quote: The sensor types are not confirmed, so camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other options all had to be covered.

facts.text: The virtual job-site research aimed to compare every method for creating virtual 3D off-road job-site environments for testing sensors and machine behaviour, including environments built from existing machine recordings.
facts.quote: compare every method for creating virtual 3D environments of off-road job sites that can be used to test sensors and machine behaviour, including environments built from recordings the machines already make

facts.text: The virtual job-site research had to consider hand-built 3D models, procedural generation, drone or ground photogrammetry, lidar survey, reconstruction from machine video or sensor recordings, neural and generative methods, reuse of site plans, terrain models, mine plans or building models, and ready-made asset libraries. Any additional method identified had to be added.
facts.quote: neural and generative methods; reuse of existing site plans, terrain models, mine plans or building models; and ready-made asset libraries. Any method not on the list was to be added.

facts.text: For each virtual job-site creation method, the research was to assess required inputs, effort per site, cost level, geometric accuracy, visual realism, editability of terrain and objects, accuracy of new sensor positions and heights, and support for moving people and vehicles.
facts.quote: the required inputs, the effort per site, the cost level, the geometric accuracy, the visual realism, whether terrain and objects can be edited afterwards, whether views from new sensor positions and heights stay accurate, and the support for moving people and vehicles

facts.text: The virtual job-site research was to investigate what test environments need beyond appearance, including material properties for each sensor type, ground properties, collision geometry and labels.
facts.quote: What does an environment need beyond appearance to be useful for testing, considering material properties for each sensor type, ground properties, collision geometry and labels?

facts.text: The virtual job-site research was to investigate whether field-machine recordings of video, sensor data, position and motion can become usable test environments, the recording quality needed, and causes of conversion failure.
facts.quote: Can recordings from machines in the field (video, sensor data, position and motion data) be turned into usable test environments, what recording quality is needed, and what makes the conversion fail?

facts.text: The virtual job-site research was to investigate how teams determine how many environments are enough and compare exact copies of real sites with a smaller set of representative site types varied by parameters.
facts.quote: How do teams decide how many environments are enough, and how do exact copies of real sites compare with a smaller set of representative site types that can be varied by parameters?

facts.text: The virtual job-site research was to identify published examples from mining, construction, quarrying, agriculture and forestry.
facts.quote: Which published examples exist for mining, construction, quarrying, agriculture or forestry?

facts.text: The virtual job-site research was required to remain neutral across vendors, products and technologies and cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.
facts.quote: The research was to stay neutral across vendors, products and technologies and to cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.

facts.text: Each important claim in the virtual job-site research was to be labelled as supported by an independent study, standard or third-party test; a vendor's own claim; or expert opinion.
facts.quote: Each important claim was to be labelled by its type of evidence (independent study, standard or third-party test; the vendor's own claim; or expert opinion)

facts.text: Each source in the virtual job-site research was to be dated, with a preference for sources from 2023 or later for tools and products.
facts.quote: each source was to be dated, with a preference for sources from 2023 or later for tools and products

facts.text: The virtual job-site research was required to report failures, limits and evidence against each approach, not only successes.
facts.quote: Failures, limits and evidence against each approach were to be reported, not only successes.

facts.text: The virtual job-site research was required to flag evidence proven only for on-road vehicles as on-road-only evidence.
facts.quote: Anything proven only for on-road vehicles had to be flagged as such

facts.text: Where the virtual job-site research could find no information, the required answer was “not found,” rather than a guessed number, price or timeline.
facts.quote: where nothing could be found the answer was to be "not found" rather than a guessed number, price or timeline
